report.source_text: Physical examination: The general condition was good, and there were no abnormalities in the system inspection. Specialized examination: Bilateral breasts are symmetrical, with average breast development. Bilateral nipples were normal and there was no nipple discharge. A red and swollen area of 3 cm × 2 cm in size could be seen in the left armpit, accompanied by ulceration and a small amount of secretions (Fig. 1A). A mass of approximately 3.0 cm × 2.0 cm in size could be palpated in the left armpit, which was hard and had a clear boundary, with moderate activity. No obvious abnormal mass could be palpated in the right breast, and no obvious enlarged lymph nodes could be palpated in the right armpit.

report.source_text: The postoperative pathology of the left axillary mass combined with morphological and immunohistochemical results was consistent with Paget disease. The pathological examination of the skin lesions showed an abundance of keratinization in the epidermis, a large number of atypical cells in the epithelial layer, infiltration of interstitial lymphocytes, and infiltration of Paget cells in the superficial dermis (Fig. 2). Postoperative immunohistochemistry showed estrogen receptor (+, 20%), progesterone receptor (−), human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (3+), Ki-67 (30%), cytokine (CK)7 (+), and p63 (−) (Fig. 3).

report.source_text: The patient was placed in a supine position and under general anesthesia, left subaxillary mass resection, freezing and left breast cancer breast conserving surgery was performed. We covered the affected area with gauze before cutting the skin and fix the skin. We made a shuttle shaped incision 1.5 cm outside the lesion area, approximately 7 cm in length, and separated toward the deep. During the surgery, the size of the tissue, including the lesion, was approximately 7 cm × 5 cm and frozen during the surgery (Fig. 1B). The results showed that fibrous adipose tissue can be seen in the left armpit, and a large number of inflammatory cells infiltrate. The diagnosis was to be confirmed by paraffin section. The postoperative pathology of the left axillary mass combined with morphological and immunohistochemical results was consistent with Paget disease. The pathological examination of the skin lesions showed an abundance of keratinization in the epidermis, a large number of atypical cells in the epithelial layer, infiltration of interstitial lymphocytes, and infiltration of Paget cells in the superficial dermis (Fig. 2). Postoperative immunohistochemistry showed estrogen receptor (+, 20%), progesterone receptor (−), human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (3+), Ki-67 (30%), cytokine (CK)7 (+), and p63 (−) (Fig. 3). The patient incision healed well after surgery and did not undergo chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

report.source_text: Following up for 16 months, there has been no local recurrence, no swelling of the right axillary lymph node, no distant metastasis found on follow-up, and no complications such as upper limb lymphedema, upper limb sensory abnormalities, or motor disorders have been observed.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Paget disease (extramammary Paget disease of the axilla)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old female presented with a 2-year history of a left axillary mass that had recently increased in size and ulcerated. Physical examination revealed a 3 cm × 2 cm red, swollen, ulcerated area with secretions and a palpable hard mass with clear boundaries. Preoperative breast MRI showed no obvious abnormalities, while ultrasound demonstrated bilateral adenosis (BI-RADS 2), bilateral lipomas, and left axillary lymph node enlargement. The patient underwent left subaxillary mass resection (7 cm × 5 cm tissue) with intraoperative frozen section showing fibrous adipose tissue with inflammatory infiltrate. Postoperative pathology confirmed Paget disease, showing epidermal keratinization, atypical cells in the epithelial layer, interstitial lymphocyte infiltration, and Paget cells in the superficial dermis. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated ER (+, 20%), PR (−), HER2 (3+), Ki-67 (30%), CK7 (+), and p63 (−). The pathology was specifically classified as 'Paget disease outside the armpit breast' (extramammary Paget disease). Postoperatively, the incision healed well without chemotherapy or radiotherapy. At 16-month follow-up, there was no local recurrence, no contralateral axillary lymphadenopathy, no distant metastasis, and no complications.
